findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on datetime sort keys (auditlog optimized_pagination path)
findings.body: The auditlog endpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime', but get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil to the raw attribute value. That attribute is a datetime, so math.floor raises TypeError. build_cursor calls key(results[0]) whenever cursor.value is 0 and there are results, so the first page of any superuser or global-access request with optimized_pagination=true and at least one audit log returns a 500. value_from_cursor also returns the raw integer cursor value, which build_queryset would compare against a datetime column on later pages. The paginator needs DateTimePaginator-style handling (strftime/timestamp conversion) or the endpoint must not route datetime keys to it.

findings.title: Negative-offset branch relies on Django negative slicing, which is unsupported
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, the code slices queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start. Django QuerySet.__getitem__ rejects negative indices ('Negative indexing is not supported'), so this raises instead of returning data. The comment 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false, and the claim 'This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' is unsupported. Any admin request with a crafted cursor carrying a negative offset gets a 500, and the feature the branch advertises does not work.

findings.title: Previous-page cursor with negative offset still passes a negative start index to queryset slicing
findings.body: For is_prev cursors, start_offset is set to the raw offset, which Cursor.from_string allows to be negative from user input. The slice queryset[start_offset:stop] then raises on a negative index, so a user-supplied cursor such as '0:-1:1' produces a 500. The crash predates this PR, but the PR adds a comment at lines 179-181 calling this behavior safe and intentional, and clamps only the next-page direction, so the inconsistency is now written down as design.

findings.title: Span eviction at 1000 is silent: no log or metric when spans are dropped
findings.body: When span_count exceeds 1000, zpopmin silently removes the lowest-scored (oldest by end timestamp) spans from the segment. The Python side previously logged 'Skipping too large segment' and emitted spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded, and that guard was removed in buffer.py. Dropped spans are now invisible to operators, and the limit is hardcoded here rather than configured. Emit a metric (and ideally a log) from the script or the caller when eviction occurs.

findings.title: Key type change from Redis set to sorted set breaks in-flight buffers during deploy
findings.body: The span-buf:s:* keys change from SET to ZSET but keep the same name prefix. Any segment key written by the old code is a SET. After deploy, ZADD in process_spans, ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE in add-buffer.lua, and ZSCAN in _load_segment_data all fail with WRONGTYPE. Ingestion raises for those traces, and flush_segments raises before done_flush_segments runs, so the queue entries are not cleared until the keys expire (redis_ttl, default 3600s). The PR needs a new key prefix or a drain/migration plan.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE uses default SUM aggregation, doubling scores of duplicate payloads
findings.body: zunionstore is called without AGGREGATE, so the default SUM applies. When the same payload already exists in the destination (for example a redelivered Kafka message, or a span present in both merged sets), its score becomes the sum of the two end timestamps. That corrupts the eviction ordering, which relies on score = end_timestamp_precise. Use AGGREGATE MIN or MAX so the score is preserved.

findings.title: Redirect-chain depth limit silently reduced from 10000 to 1000 and caveat comment removed
findings.body: The loop bound changed from 10000 to 1000 with no mention in the PR description, and the comment explaining the limit's consequence was deleted. Redirect chains deeper than 1000 are now cut off silently, so their spans are attached to an intermediate segment rather than the root. Either keep the old limit or document the change and keep the caveat.

findings.title: Hard key access on end_timestamp_precise can fail an entire batch
findings.body: val['end_timestamp_precise'] is a strict lookup, and the cast(SpanEvent, ...) is type-only and does not validate anything at runtime. Before this PR the field was not read. A single message missing it raises KeyError inside process_batch, which fails the whole batch and can leave the consumer retrying the same poison batch. Use val.get with a fallback, or validate and skip the bad message with a metric.

findings.title: max_segment_spans config is now dead and disagrees with the hardcoded Lua limit
findings.body: After this PR the span-count check in _load_segment_data was removed, so the max_segment_spans constructor argument (default 1001) is never read. The effective limit is the hardcoded 1000 in add-buffer.lua. Configuration that appears to control the limit no longer does, and the two defaults disagree. Remove the parameter or wire it into the script.

findings.title: No test covers the new 1000-span eviction, the set-to-zset change, or the redirect depth change
findings.body: The headline feature of this PR, evicting spans beyond 1000 during insert, has no test. The added lines only add end_timestamp_precise to existing fixtures, so nothing checks that the segment is capped, that the oldest spans are the ones evicted, that merges keep the right scores, or that the loop limit behaves as intended. Add tests that insert more than 1000 spans through process_spans and assert the resulting count and which payloads survive.

findings.title: optimized_pagination path is untested and crashes on the first page
findings.body: The new branch gated by optimized_pagination=true has no test. Such a test would immediately expose the datetime TypeError in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key, so the endpoint's new path is broken and unverified. Add a test for a superuser request with that parameter and at least one audit log entry.

findings.title: Comment claims a negative-offset feature that this change does not implement
findings.body: The added comment says Cursor now allows negative offsets for advanced pagination and enables reverse pagination from arbitrary positions. The diff changes nothing in this constructor (self.offset = int(offset) is unchanged), and the paginators that consume negative offsets crash on them. The comment describes behavior that does not exist, so it should be removed or corrected.

findings.title: Module docstring still describes span-buf:s:* keys as sets
findings.body: The glossary says span-buf:s:* are 'the actual set keys', but after this PR they are sorted sets (ZADD, ZUNIONSTORE, ZSCAN, ZPOPMIN). Update the docstring so future readers do not assume SET commands.

findings.title: Unrelated pagination changes and an undocumented query parameter are bundled into a spans PR
findings.body: The PR title is about span buffer eviction, but this file, paginator.py, and cursors.py add an experimental audit-log paginator switch. That switch is an undocumented optimized_pagination query parameter, and the PR description is just 'Test 2', so reviewers have no rationale for it. Split these changes into their own PR with a description, or revert them from this one.
